title: Architectural Review Board approves 21 West Swan Avenue garage with freeze board added

Architectural Review Board approves 21 West Swan Avenue garage with freeze board added
Bill Sharp of Coach House and homeowner Nich presented the detached garage replacement, which the board approved after requiring the trim to match the existing house.
The Architectural Review Board approved a replacement detached garage at 21 West Swan Avenue on Thursday, Oct. 1, with the condition that a freeze board be added to match the original structure.
THE QUESTION OF TRIM During the work session, a board member raised a question about the siding and trim noted in the plans, asking whether it referred to the existing garage being removed or to the existing house. Another member noted the discrepancy in the fascia depth, saying it "looks like that fascia is deeper than six."
THE HEARING At the public hearing, Bill Sharp of Coach House and homeowner Nich appeared before the board. A board member identified as Carol explained the reasoning for matching details to the house, saying, "I think picking up those nice details would would help tie the two together." Sharp confirmed a freeze board had been on the original garage in photos and agreed to add it, saying "I'll add the freeze board."
THE VOTE The board approved the project by voice vote. The motion was "to approve 21 West Swan with the understanding that the sighting uh and trim dimensions will match the existing house and that a freeze board will be added to the garage to match." The motion passed with one member opposed.
NEXT STEPS After the vote, Nich asked when a permit might be expected. A board member explained that recommendations would be sent out the next day. After that, the project would go to the building plan reviewer, identified as Jim, for any further comments or concerns.
